records.name: display
records.title: display CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The display CSS property sets whether an element is treated as a block or inline box and the layout used for its children, such as flow layout, grid or flex.

records.name: order
records.title: order CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The order CSS property sets the order to lay out an item in a flex or grid container. Items in a container are sorted by ascending order value and then by their source code order. Items not given an explicit order value are assigned the default value of 0.

records.name: reading-flow
records.title: reading-flow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The reading-flow CSS property enables modifying the reading order of child elements of a block, flex, or grid layout. This affects the order in which they are rendered to speech and navigated to when using sequential navigation such as tabbing to links or buttons.

records.name: reading-order
records.title: reading-order CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The reading-order CSS property enables changing the order in which a child of a reading flow container is read relative to its element siblings.

records.name: visibility
records.title: visibility CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The visibility CSS property shows or hides an element without changing the layout of a document. The property can also hide rows or columns in a <table>.

records.name: align-content
records.title: align-content CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The CSS align-content property sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis.

records.name: align-items
records.title: align-items CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The CSS align-items property sets the align-self value on all direct children as a group. In flexbox, it controls the alignment of items on the cross axis. In grid layout, it controls the alignment of items on the block axis within their grid areas.

records.name: align-self
records.title: align-self CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The align-self CSS property overrides a grid or flex item's align-items value. In grid, it aligns the item inside the grid area. In flexbox, it aligns the item on the cross axis.

records.name: column-gap
records.title: column-gap CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-gap CSS property sets the size of the gap (gutter) between an element's columns in multi-column, flexible box, and grid layouts.

records.name: gap
records.title: gap CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The gap CSS shorthand property sets the gaps (also called gutters) between rows and columns on multi-column, flex, and grid containers.

records.name: justify-content
records.title: justify-content CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The CSS justify-content property defines how the browser distributes space between and around content items along the main axis of a flex container and the inline axis of grid and multicol containers.

records.name: justify-items
records.title: justify-items CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The CSS justify-items property defines the default justify-self for all items of the box, giving them all a default way of justifying each box along the appropriate axis.

records.name: justify-self
records.title: justify-self CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The CSS justify-self property sets the way a box is justified inside its alignment container along the appropriate axis.

records.name: place-content
records.title: place-content CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The place-content CSS shorthand property allows you to align content along both the block and inline directions at once (i.e., the align-content and justify-content properties) in a relevant layout system such as Grid or Flexbox.

records.name: place-items
records.title: place-items CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The place-items CSS shorthand property aligns items along both block and inline directions at the same time.

records.name: place-self
records.title: place-self CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The place-self CSS shorthand property allows you to align an individual item in both the block and inline directions at once (i.e., the align-self and justify-self properties). This property applies to block-level boxes, absolutely-positioned boxes, and grid items. If the second value is not present, the first value is also used for it.

records.name: row-gap
records.title: row-gap CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The row-gap CSS property sets the size of the gap (gutter) between an element's rows in multi-column, flexible box, and grid layouts.

records.name: flex
records.title: flex CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex CSS shorthand property sets how a flex item will grow or shrink to fit the space available in its flex container.

records.name: flex-basis
records.title: flex-basis CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-basis CSS property sets the initial main size of a flex item. It sets the size of the content box unless otherwise set with box-sizing.

records.name: flex-direction
records.title: flex-direction CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-direction CSS property sets how flex items are placed in the flex container defining the main axis and the direction (normal or reversed).

records.name: flex-flow
records.title: flex-flow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-flow CSS shorthand property specifies the direction of a flex container, as well as its wrapping behavior.

records.name: flex-grow
records.title: flex-grow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-grow CSS property sets the flex grow factor, which specifies how much of the flex container's positive free space, if any, should be assigned to the flex item's main size.

records.name: flex-line-count
records.title: flex-line-count CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: Sets the minimum number of flex lines over which wrapped items are balanced. It has an effect only when flex-wrap or flex-flow includes the balance keyword in a multi-line flex container.
records.supportLabel: Experimental; CSS Flexible Box Layout Level 2 Editor’s Draft

records.name: flex-shrink
records.title: flex-shrink CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-shrink CSS property sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item. If the size of all flex items is larger than the flex container, the flex items can shrink to fit according to their flex-shrink value. Each flex line's negative free space is distributed between the line's flex items that have a flex-shrink value greater than 0.

records.name: flex-wrap
records.title: flex-wrap CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The flex-wrap CSS property sets whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. If wrapping is allowed, it sets the direction that lines are stacked.

records.name: grid
records.title: grid CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid CSS shorthand property sets all of the explicit and implicit grid properties in a single declaration.

records.name: grid-area
records.title: grid-area CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-area CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the edges of its grid area.

records.name: grid-auto-columns
records.title: grid-auto-columns CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-auto-columns CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid column track or pattern of tracks.

records.name: grid-auto-flow
records.title: grid-auto-flow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-auto-flow CSS property controls how the auto-placement algorithm works, specifying exactly how auto-placed items get flowed into the grid.

records.name: grid-auto-rows
records.title: grid-auto-rows CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-auto-rows CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid row track or pattern of tracks.

records.name: grid-column
records.title: grid-column CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-column CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its grid area.

records.name: grid-column-end
records.title: grid-column-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-column-end CSS property specifies a grid item's end position within the grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the block-end edge of its grid area.

records.name: grid-column-start
records.title: grid-column-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-column-start CSS property specifies a grid item's start position within the grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement. This start position defines the block-start edge of the grid area.

records.name: grid-row
records.title: grid-row CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-row CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its grid area.

records.name: grid-row-end
records.title: grid-row-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-row-end CSS property specifies a grid item's end position within the grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-end edge of its grid area.

records.name: grid-row-start
records.title: grid-row-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-row-start CSS property specifies a grid item's start position within the grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start edge of its grid area.

records.name: grid-template
records.title: grid-template CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-template CSS shorthand property specifies the grid columns, grid rows, and grid areas.

records.name: grid-template-areas
records.title: grid-template-areas CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-template-areas CSS property specifies named grid areas, establishing the cells in the grid and assigning them names.

records.name: grid-template-columns
records.title: grid-template-columns CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-template-columns CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid columns.

records.name: grid-template-rows
records.title: grid-template-rows CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The grid-template-rows CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid rows.

records.name: bottom
records.title: bottom CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The bottom CSS property participates in setting the vertical position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

records.name: clear
records.title: clear CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The clear CSS property sets whether an element must be moved below (cleared) floating elements that precede it. The clear property applies to floating and non-floating elements.

records.name: float
records.title: float CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The float CSS property places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around it. The element is removed from the normal flow of the page, though still remaining a part of the flow (in contrast to absolute positioning).

records.name: inset
records.title: inset CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset CSS shorthand property corresponds to the top, right, bottom, and/or left properties. It has the same multi-value syntax of the margin shorthand.

records.name: inset-block
records.title: inset-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end offsets of an element, which maps to physical offsets depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top and bottom, or right and left properties depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: inset-block-end
records.title: inset-block-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-block-end CSS property defines the logical block end offset of an element, which maps to a physical inset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top, right, bottom, or left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: inset-block-start
records.title: inset-block-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-block-start CSS property defines the logical block start offset of an element, which maps to a physical inset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top, right, bottom, or left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: inset-inline
records.title: inset-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-inline CSS shorthand property defines the logical start and end offsets of an element in the inline direction, which maps to physical offsets depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top and bottom, or right and left properties depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: inset-inline-end
records.title: inset-inline-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-inline-end CSS property defines the logical inline end inset of an element, which maps to a physical offset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top, right, bottom, or left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: inset-inline-start
records.title: inset-inline-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The inset-inline-start CSS property defines the logical inline start inset of an element, which maps to a physical offset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the top, right, bottom, or left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: left
records.title: left CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The left CSS property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

records.name: position
records.title: position CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position CSS property sets how an element is positioned in a document. The top, right, bottom, and left physical properties and the inset-block-start, inset-block-end, inset-inline-start, and inset-inline-end flow-relative logical properties can be used to determine the final location of positioned elements.

records.name: right
records.title: right CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The right CSS property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

records.name: top
records.title: top CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The top CSS property sets the vertical position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

records.name: z-index
records.title: z-index CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The z-index CSS property sets the z-order of a positioned element and its descendants or flex and grid items. Overlapping elements with a larger z-index cover those with a smaller one.

records.name: -webkit-line-clamp
records.title: Page not found | MDN
records.description: Legacy prefixed line-clamping property. Its interoperable legacy behavior requires display: -webkit-box or -webkit-inline-box, -webkit-box-orient: vertical, and overflow: hidden; prefer the unprefixed line-clamp when its support meets the project need.
records.supportLabel: Legacy WebKit-compatible behavior; see line-clamp compatibility

records.name: line-clamp
records.title: line-clamp CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The line-clamp CSS property allows limiting of the contents of a block to the specified number of lines. Optionally, it also allows inserting content into the last line to indicate that content was truncated.

records.name: overflow
records.title: overflow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow CSS shorthand property sets the desired behavior when content does not fit in the element's padding box (overflows) in the horizontal and/or vertical direction.

records.name: overflow-block
records.title: overflow-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-block CSS property sets what shows when content overflows the block start and block end edges of a box. This may be nothing, a scroll bar, or the overflow content.

records.name: overflow-clip-margin
records.title: overflow-clip-margin CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-clip-margin CSS property determines how far outside its bounds an element with overflow: clip may be painted before being clipped. The bound defined by this property is called the overflow clip edge of the box.

records.name: overflow-inline
records.title: overflow-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-inline CSS property sets what shows when content overflows the inline start and end edges of a box. This may be nothing, a scroll bar, or the overflow content.

records.name: overflow-x
records.title: overflow-x CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-x CSS property sets what shows when content overflows a block-level element's left and right edges. This may be nothing, a scroll bar, or the overflow content. This property may also be set by using the overflow shorthand property.

records.name: overflow-y
records.title: overflow-y CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-y CSS property sets what shows when content overflows a block-level element's top and bottom edges. This may be nothing, a scroll bar, or the overflow content. This property may also be set by using the overflow shorthand property.

records.name: scroll-axis-lock
records.title: Page not found | MDN
records.description: Draft CSS Overflow property that tells the user agent whether it may lock a scroll gesture on the element to one axis. The proposed values are auto and none; it applies to scroll containers and is not a stable cross-browser baseline.
records.supportLabel: W3C Editor’s Draft; experimental and support varies

records.name: scroll-behavior
records.title: scroll-behavior CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-behavior CSS property sets the behavior for a scrolling box when scrolling is triggered by the navigation or CSSOM scrolling APIs.

records.name: scroll-marker-group
records.title: scroll-marker-group CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-marker-group CSS property controls whether a scroll container element has a ::scroll-marker-group pseudo-element generated. If present, the property also specifies whether the scroll marker group should be placed before or after the contents of the scroll group container in the default visual and tab order.

records.name: scroll-target-group
records.title: scroll-target-group CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-target-group CSS property specifies whether an element is a scroll marker group container.

records.name: scrollbar-gutter
records.title: scrollbar-gutter CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scrollbar-gutter CSS property allows authors to reserve space for the scrollbar, preventing unwanted layout changes as the content grows while also avoiding unnecessary visuals when scrolling isn't needed.

records.name: text-overflow
records.title: text-overflow CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The text-overflow CSS property sets how hidden overflow content is signaled to users.

records.name: scroll-margin
records.title: scroll-margin CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin CSS shorthand property sets all of the scroll margins of an element at once, assigning values much like the margin property does for margins of an element.

records.name: scroll-margin-block
records.title: scroll-margin-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-block CSS shorthand property sets the scroll margins of an element in the block dimension.

records.name: scroll-margin-block-end
records.title: scroll-margin-block-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-block-end property defines the margin of the scroll snap area at the end of the block dimension that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-block-start
records.title: scroll-margin-block-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-block-start property defines the margin of the scroll snap area at the start of the block dimension that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-bottom
records.title: scroll-margin-bottom CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-bottom property defines the bottom margin of the scroll snap area that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-inline
records.title: scroll-margin-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-inline CSS shorthand property sets the scroll margins of an element in the inline dimension.

records.name: scroll-margin-inline-end
records.title: scroll-margin-inline-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-inline-end property defines the margin of the scroll snap area at the end of the inline dimension that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-inline-start
records.title: scroll-margin-inline-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-inline-start property defines the margin of the scroll snap area at the start of the inline dimension that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-left
records.title: scroll-margin-left CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-left property defines the left margin of the scroll snap area that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-right
records.title: scroll-margin-right CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-right property defines the right margin of the scroll snap area that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-margin-top
records.title: scroll-margin-top CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-margin-top property defines the top margin of the scroll snap area that is used for snapping this box to the snapport. The scroll snap area is determined by taking the transformed border box, finding its rectangular bounding box (axis-aligned in the scroll container's coordinate space), then adding the specified outsets.

records.name: scroll-padding
records.title: scroll-padding CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding CSS shorthand property sets scroll padding on all sides of an element at once. It specifies offsets that define the optimal viewing region of a scrollport within a scroll container.

records.name: scroll-padding-block
records.title: scroll-padding-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-block CSS shorthand property sets the scroll padding of an element in the block dimension.

records.name: scroll-padding-block-end
records.title: scroll-padding-block-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-block-end property defines offsets for the end edge in the block dimension of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-block-start
records.title: scroll-padding-block-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-block-start property defines offsets for the start edge in the block dimension of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-bottom
records.title: scroll-padding-bottom CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-bottom property defines offsets for the bottom of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-inline
records.title: scroll-padding-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-inline CSS shorthand property sets the scroll padding of an element in the inline dimension.

records.name: scroll-padding-inline-end
records.title: scroll-padding-inline-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-inline-end property defines offsets for the end edge in the inline dimension of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-inline-start
records.title: scroll-padding-inline-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-inline-start property defines offsets for the start edge in the inline dimension of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-left
records.title: scroll-padding-left CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-left property defines offsets for the left of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-right
records.title: scroll-padding-right CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-right property defines offsets for the right of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-padding-top
records.title: scroll-padding-top CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-padding-top property defines offsets for the top of the optimal viewing region of the scrollport: the region used as the target region for placing things in view of the user. This allows the author to exclude regions of the scrollport that are obscured by other content (such as fixed-positioned toolbars or sidebars) or to put more breathing room between a targeted element and the edges of the scrollport.

records.name: scroll-snap-align
records.title: scroll-snap-align CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-snap-align CSS property specifies the box's snap position as an alignment of its snap area.

records.name: scroll-snap-stop
records.title: scroll-snap-stop CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-snap-stop CSS property defines whether or not the scroll container is allowed to "pass over" possible snap positions.

records.name: scroll-snap-type
records.title: scroll-snap-type CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-snap-type CSS property is set on a scroll container, opting it into scroll snapping by setting the direction and strictness of snap point enforcement within the snap port.

records.name: column-count
records.title: column-count CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-count CSS property breaks an element's content into the specified number of columns.

records.name: column-fill
records.title: column-fill CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-fill CSS property controls how an element's contents are balanced when broken into columns.

records.name: column-rule
records.title: column-rule CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-rule CSS shorthand property sets the width, style, and color of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.

records.name: column-rule-color
records.title: column-rule-color CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-rule-color CSS property defines the colors of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.

records.name: column-rule-style
records.title: column-rule-style CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-rule-style CSS property defines the line style of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.

records.name: column-rule-width
records.title: column-rule-width CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-rule-width CSS property defines the widths of the lines drawn between columns in multi-column grid, flex, and multi-col layouts.

records.name: column-span
records.title: column-span CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The column-span CSS property makes it possible for an element to span across all columns when its value is set to all.

records.name: columns
records.title: columns CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The columns CSS shorthand property sets the maximum number of columns to use when drawing an element's contents, along with the minimum width and maximum height of the element's columns.

records.name: box-decoration-break
records.title: box-decoration-break CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The box-decoration-break CSS property specifies how an element's fragments should be rendered when broken across multiple lines, columns, or pages.

records.name: break-after
records.title: break-after CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The break-after CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave after a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.

records.name: break-before
records.title: break-before CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The break-before CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave before a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.

records.name: break-inside
records.title: break-inside CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The break-inside CSS property sets how page, column, or region breaks should behave inside a generated box. If there is no generated box, the property is ignored.

records.name: orphans
records.title: orphans CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The orphans CSS property sets the minimum number of lines in a block container that must be shown at the bottom of a page, region, or column.

records.name: widows
records.title: widows CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The widows CSS property sets the minimum number of lines in a block container that must be shown at the top of a page, region, or column.

records.name: border-collapse
records.title: border-collapse CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The border-collapse CSS property sets whether cells inside a <table> have shared or separate borders.

records.name: border-spacing
records.title: border-spacing CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The border-spacing CSS property sets the distance between the borders of adjacent cells in a <table>. This property applies only when border-collapse is separate.

records.name: caption-side
records.title: caption-side CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The caption-side CSS property puts the content of a table's <caption> on the specified side. The values are relative to the writing-mode of the table.

records.name: empty-cells
records.title: empty-cells CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The empty-cells CSS property sets whether borders and backgrounds appear around <table> cells that have no visible content.

records.name: table-layout
records.title: table-layout CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The table-layout CSS property sets the algorithm used to lay out <table> cells, rows, and columns.

records.name: contain
records.title: contain CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description:
The contain CSS property indicates that an element and its contents are, as much as possible, independent from the rest of the document tree.
Containment enables isolating a subsection of the DOM, providing performance benefits by limiting calculations of layout, style, paint, size, or any combination to a DOM subtree rather than the entire page. Containment can also be used to scope CSS counters and quotes.

records.name: content-visibility
records.title: content-visibility CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The content-visibility CSS property controls whether or not an element renders its contents at all, along with forcing a strong set of containments, allowing user agents to potentially omit large swathes of layout and rendering work until it becomes needed. It enables the user agent to skip an element's rendering work (including layout and painting) until it is needed — which makes the initial page load much faster.

records.name: container
records.title: container CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The container shorthand CSS property establishes the element as a query container and specifies the name and type of the containment context used in a container query.

records.name: container-name
records.title: container-name CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The container-name CSS property specifies a list of query container names used by the @container at-rule in a container query.

records.name: container-type
records.title: container-type CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The container-type CSS property specifies the type of container context used in a container query.

records.name: overscroll-behavior
records.title: overscroll-behavior CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overscroll-behavior CSS property controls what happens when scrolling reaches the edge of a scroll container.

records.name: overscroll-behavior-block
records.title: overscroll-behavior-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overscroll-behavior-block CSS property sets the browser's behavior when the block direction boundary of a scrolling area is reached.

records.name: overscroll-behavior-inline
records.title: overscroll-behavior-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overscroll-behavior-inline CSS property sets the browser's behavior when the inline direction boundary of a scrolling area is reached.

records.name: overscroll-behavior-x
records.title: overscroll-behavior-x CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overscroll-behavior-x CSS property sets the browser's behavior when the horizontal boundary of a scrolling area is reached.

records.name: overscroll-behavior-y
records.title: overscroll-behavior-y CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overscroll-behavior-y CSS property sets the browser's behavior when the vertical boundary of a scrolling area is reached.

records.name: scrollbar-color
records.title: scrollbar-color CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scrollbar-color CSS property sets the color of the scrollbar track and thumb.

records.name: scrollbar-width
records.title: scrollbar-width CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scrollbar-width property allows the author to set the desired thickness of an element's scrollbars when they are shown.

records.name: direction
records.title: direction CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The direction CSS property sets the direction of text, table and grid columns, and horizontal overflow. Use rtl for languages written from right to left (like Hebrew or Arabic), and ltr for those written from left to right (like English and most other languages).

records.name: text-combine-upright
records.title: text-combine-upright CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The text-combine-upright CSS property sets the combination of characters into the space of a single character. If the combined text is wider than 1em, the user agent must fit the contents within 1em. The resulting composition is treated as a single upright glyph for layout and decoration. This property only has an effect in vertical writing modes.

records.name: text-orientation
records.title: text-orientation CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The text-orientation CSS property sets the orientation of the text characters in a line. It only affects text in vertical mode (when writing-mode is not horizontal-tb). It is useful for controlling the display of languages that use vertical script, and also for making vertical table headers.

records.name: unicode-bidi
records.title: unicode-bidi CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The unicode-bidi CSS property, together with the direction property, determines how bidirectional text in a document is handled. For example, if a block of content contains both left-to-right and right-to-left text, the user-agent uses a complex Unicode algorithm to decide how to display the text. The unicode-bidi property overrides this algorithm and allows the developer to control the text embedding.

records.name: writing-mode
records.title: writing-mode CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The writing-mode CSS property sets whether lines of text are laid out horizontally or vertically, as well as the direction in which text flows.

records.name: block-size
records.title: block-size CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The block-size CSS property defines the size of an element's block along the block axis. If the writing-mode is horizontal, it corresponds to the height; if the writing mode is vertical, it corresponds to the width. A related property is inline-size, which defines the other dimension of the element.

records.name: border-block
records.title: border-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The border-block CSS shorthand property sets the individual logical block border property values in a single place in the style sheet.

records.name: border-block-color
records.title: border-block-color CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The border-block-color CSS property defines the color of the logical block borders of an element, which maps to a physical border color depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the border-top-color and border-bottom-color, or border-right-color and border-left-color property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

If the writing-mode is horizontal, it corresponds to the width; if the writing mode is vertical, it corresponds to the height. A related property is block-size, which defines the other dimension of the element.

records.name: margin-block
records.title: margin-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end margins of an element, which maps to physical margins depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: margin-block-end
records.title: margin-block-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-block-end CSS property defines the logical block end margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: margin-block-start
records.title: margin-block-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-block-start CSS property defines the logical block start margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: margin-inline
records.title: margin-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-inline CSS shorthand property defines both the logical inline start and end margins of an element, which maps to physical margins depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: margin-inline-end
records.title: margin-inline-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-inline-end CSS property defines the logical inline end margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. In other words, it corresponds to the margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom or margin-left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: margin-inline-start
records.title: margin-inline-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The margin-inline-start CSS property defines the logical inline start margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation. It corresponds to the margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom, or margin-left property depending on the values defined for writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

records.name: max-block-size
records.title: max-block-size CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The max-block-size CSS property specifies the maximum size of an element in the direction opposite that of the writing direction as specified by writing-mode. That is, if the writing direction is horizontal, then max-block-size is equivalent to max-height; if the writing direction is vertical, max-block-size is the same as max-width.

records.name: max-inline-size
records.title: max-inline-size CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The max-inline-size CSS property defines the horizontal or vertical maximum size of an element's block, depending on its writing mode. It corresponds to either the max-width or the max-height property, depending on the value of writing-mode.

records.name: min-block-size
records.title: min-block-size CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The min-block-size CSS property defines the minimum horizontal or vertical size of an element's block, depending on its writing mode. It corresponds to either the min-width or the min-height property, depending on the value of writing-mode.

records.name: min-inline-size
records.title: min-inline-size CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The min-inline-size CSS property defines the horizontal or vertical minimal size of an element's block, depending on its writing mode. It corresponds to either the min-width or the min-height property, depending on the value of writing-mode.

records.name: padding-block
records.title: padding-block CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The padding-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end padding of an element, which maps to physical padding properties depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: padding-block-end
records.title: padding-block-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The padding-block-end CSS property defines the logical block end padding of an element, which maps to a physical padding depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: padding-block-start
records.title: padding-block-start CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The padding-block-start CSS property defines the logical block start padding of an element, which maps to a physical padding depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: padding-inline
records.title: padding-inline CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The padding-inline CSS shorthand property defines the logical inline start and end padding of an element, which maps to physical padding properties depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: padding-inline-end
records.title: padding-inline-end CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The padding-inline-end CSS property defines the logical inline end padding of an element, which maps to a physical padding depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.description: The padding-inline-start CSS property defines the logical inline start padding of an element, which maps to a physical padding depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

records.name: overflow-anchor
records.title: overflow-anchor CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overflow-anchor CSS property provides a way to opt out of the browser's scroll anchoring behavior, which adjusts scroll position to minimize content shifts.

records.name: zoom
records.title: zoom CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description:
The zoom CSS property can be used to control the magnification level of an element.
transform: scale() can be used as an alternative to this property.

records.name: overlay
records.title: overlay CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The overlay CSS property specifies whether an element appearing in the top layer (for example, a shown popover or modal <dialog> element) is actually rendered in the top layer. This property is only relevant within a list of transition-property values, and only if allow-discrete is set as the transition-behavior.

records.name: anchor-name
records.title: anchor-name CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The anchor-name CSS property enables defining an element as an anchor element by giving it one or more identifying anchor names. Each name can then be set as the value of a positioned element's position-anchor property to associate it with the anchor.

records.name: anchor-scope
records.title: anchor-scope CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The anchor-scope CSS property can be used to limit the scope in which a positioned element can be associated with anchor elements to a particular subtree.

records.name: position-anchor
records.title: position-anchor CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description:
The position-anchor CSS property specifies the default anchor element for a positioned element.
This default is used by position-area and position-try, and by anchor functions (anchor() and anchor-size()) when no <anchor-name> argument is provided to those functions.

records.name: position-area
records.title: position-area CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position-area CSS property enables an anchor-positioned element to be positioned relative to the edges of its associated anchor element by placing the positioned element on one or more tiles of an implicit 3x3 grid, where the anchoring element is the center cell.

records.name: position-try
records.title: position-try CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position-try CSS shorthand property corresponds to the position-try-order and position-try-fallbacks properties.

records.name: position-try-fallbacks
records.title: position-try-fallbacks CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position-try-fallbacks CSS property enables you to specify a list of one or more alternative position try fallback options for anchor-positioned elements to be placed relative to their associated anchor elements. When the element would otherwise overflow its inset-modified containing block, the browser will try placing the positioned element in these different fallback positions, in the order provided, until it finds a value that stops it from overflowing its container or the viewport.

records.name: position-try-order
records.title: position-try-order CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position-try-order CSS property allows you to prioritize the position-try-fallbacks option applied to an anchor-positioned element when it first renders, based on which option creates the most space around the element in the given direction.

records.name: position-visibility
records.title: position-visibility CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The position-visibility CSS property enables conditionally hiding an anchor-positioned element depending on, for example, whether it is overflowing its containing element or the viewport.

records.name: max-lines
records.title: Page not found | MDN
records.description: CSS Overflow Level 4 draft longhand that sets the clamp point of a line-clamp container or forces a region break in a fragmentation container. Its draft syntax accepts auto and a positive integer; it is not a broadly interoperable standalone production feature.
records.supportLabel: W3C Editor’s Draft; experimental and support varies

records.name: scroll-initial-target
records.title: scroll-initial-target CSS property - CSS | MDN
records.description: The scroll-initial-target CSS property enables the definition of elements that are potential snap targets when their ancestor scroll container is first rendered.
